Matrix degradation by MMP9 is one of the steps by which tumour cells cross the vascular barrier into the portal vein. edges.description: Graded below the hepatitis and cirrhosis links into this same node for two reasons that are worth stating rather than leaving to inference: the cited sentence covers only the aflatoxin half of this bundled exposure and says nothing about alcohol, and it is hedged as a belief about prevalence rather than a measured interaction.

The diet is the exposure that raises hepatocyte MLKL protein in the MASLD-HCC model, and it is the only incoming edge this arm has. The measurement is made in diet-fed mice, so the edge is asserted for the model system the paper reports and not for a human dietary pattern.

Monomethyl phthalate raises MMP9 in the paper's hepatocellular carcinoma cell model, and inhibiting MMP9 removes what the exposure does to those cells. Graded as exacerbation rather than as a trigger on purpose. The experiment is run in an established hepatocellular carcinoma line, so what it demonstrates is the exposure worsening a tumour that already exists, which is how the paper titles its own finding. Reading it as a trigger would additionally enter this node as a non-mutational origin of the cancer under the cell-of-origin derivation, a claim nothing here supports. The edge is asserted for the cell model and not for a measured human exposure response: the human arm is a Mendelian randomization estimate against hepatocellular carcinoma risk, which does not measure MMP9.

nodes.description: Multiple driver genes are recurrently mutated in HCC, including TERT promoter (60%), TP53 (30%), CTNNB1 (30%), AXIN1 (10%), and ARID1A (10%). These mutations affect telomere maintenance, cell cycle control, WNT signaling, and chromatin remodeling.

HCC cells reprogram metabolism from oxidative phosphorylation to aerobic glycolysis (Warburg effect), enabling rapid ATP regeneration and providing carbon intermediates for biosynthesis. This metabolic shift is driven by oncogenic signaling (PI3K/AKT, MYC) and supports the high proliferative rate of hepatocellular carcinomas. The mechanism linking mitochondrial acetyl-CoA homeostasis to pyruvate transport and glycolytic switching remains incompletely characterized.

evidence.snippet: most cancer cells produce large amounts of lactate regardless of the availability of oxygen

Mechanistically, ACAA2 downregulation reduces mitochondrial acetyl-CoA levels, thereby decreasing mitochondrial pyruvate carrier 1 (MPC1) acetylation and accelerating its proteasomal degradation, which ultimately impairs mitochondrial pyruvate transport to promote glycolysis and cell proliferation.

nodes.description: First-line standard of care for unresectable HCC based on IMbrave150 trial. Anti-PD-L1 (atezolizumab) combined with anti-VEGF (bevacizumab) demonstrated superior overall survival compared to sorafenib. Requires adequate liver function (Child-Pugh A) and no high-risk varices. Immunotherapy trials in HCC require careful interpretation due to delayed treatment effects and potential violations of proportional hazard assumptions, which may affect the apparent magnitude of benefit from surrogate endpoints like PFS.

In MASLD-associated HCC, long-term Western diet raises hepatocyte MLKL protein. This is an abundance change, not a change in catalytic activity: MLKL is a catalytically dead pseudokinase whose established role is as the terminal executioner of necroptosis, and the observation here is that it accumulates. Hepatocyte-specific MLKL knockout mice on the same diet develop fewer and smaller tumours, so the accumulation is the entry point of this arm rather than a bystander finding. Elevated MLKL also marks worse outcome in human HCC, and pharmacological MLKL inhibition suppresses xenograft growth.

nodes.description: HCC develops in a chronically inflamed liver with an inherently immunosuppressive microenvironment. Tumor cells upregulate PD-L1, VEGF-mediated immunosuppression excludes effector T cells, and recruitment of regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and tumor-associated macrophages creates an immune-tolerant niche. The combination of anti-PD-L1 with anti-VEGF addresses both the checkpoint-mediated and VEGF-mediated immunosuppression.

nodes.description: Western diet suppresses the mitochondrial fusion protein and tumour suppressor MFN2, and hepatocyte MLKL is required for that suppression: MLKL deficiency restores MFN2 post-translationally. MFN2 is the fusion machinery itself, so its loss is a loss of mitochondrial fusion, and this node records that single molecular event. What the depleted mitochondrial network then fails to do is the node downstream.

nodes.description: Matrix metalloproteinase 9 is a secreted zinc endopeptidase that degrades basement-membrane and interstitial collagen, and it is the effector through which monomethyl phthalate exposure reaches hepatocellular carcinoma behaviour in the only study that has tested that link. The node records the abundance and activity change alone. Its standing rests on three separate observations: MMP9 is high in human hepatocellular carcinoma tissue and tracks with worse survival, monomethyl phthalate raises it in hepatocellular carcinoma cells, and blocking it removes the growth and migration the exposure produces in HuH-7. That last arm is what makes the upregulation the exposure's point of entry rather than a correlate of it. The invasion the enzyme enables is the node downstream, not this one.

nodes.description: The headline finding of this arm, and what separates it from the necroptotic cell-death route MLKL is normally invoked for: the diet-induced MLKL accumulation proceeds without detectable necroptosis activation, and removing hepatocyte MLKL leaves Western-diet inflammation, fibrosis and liver injury unchanged - the readouts a necroptosis-driven mechanism would be expected to move. MLKL instead localises to nuclear and mitochondrial compartments, consistent with the organelle-intrinsic function modelled downstream.

nodes.description: Chronic hepatocyte proliferation leads to telomere shortening, causing genomic instability. TERT promoter mutations, which are the most common HCC mutations, reactivate telomerase to enable unlimited replication. This creates a checkpoint bypass allowing survival of genetically unstable cells.

Activating mutations in CTNNB1 (beta-catenin) or inactivating mutations in AXIN1 lead to constitutive WNT pathway activation. This drives cell proliferation and is associated with a distinct molecular subclass of HCC with specific clinical features including cholestasis and immune exclusion.
